liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Casey Jones** (4 reviews): Opening with Casey Jones was unheard of in the early eighties; the reviewer calls this version excellent; Rarity of Casey Jones as show opener makes the show special as a collection item [20][21][25][28]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review, 1 other source): Weir was over the top on Good Lovin', one of the most rocking versions of the tour; Notes flag the transition between Around and Around and Good Lovin' [1][28]
- **Althea** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this Althea among the best versions ever played [20]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this Looks Like Rain among the best ever, with Garcia leads and interplay with Lesh [20]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): He's Gone runs over seventeen minutes [22]
- **Women Are Smarter** (1 review): Weir makes a cryptic comment before Women Are Smarter [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **Casey Jones**: back after 133 archived shows (693 days) [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-06-26.127526.schoeps.oade.BCE.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 170 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1984-06-26.beyerm88.holbrook.burke.81975.flac24**: source not stated; 22 songs; 157 min [4]
- **gd1984-06-26.beyerm88.holbrook.burke.81741.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 157 min [5]
- **gd1984-06-26.179126.senn.441.strizak.flac2448**: source not stated; 22 songs; 160 min [6]. Said about its sound: Second set sounds brighter and crisper; Around and Around ends abruptly and Good Lovin' fades in missing about ten seconds [6]
- **gd84-06-26.sbd.braverman.20324.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 141 min; rated 3.64/5 by 25 [16]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is described as slightly better than mediocre to good; Reviewer calls the soundboard sound poor, rating it 2 out of 5 despite accurate sourcing [21][22]

## Around the show

- Security was lax during the first night's first set; fans repeatedly hopped the fence and returned from their car [25]
- Early 6pm showtime; attendee recalls sound and lighting problems at the start, slow getting going, then lots of energy [28]
- First-show attendee recalls a man bouncing in a small tree, howling like a wolf [30]
- A bet concerned whether the Grateful Dead played Casey Jones in 1984 [40]
- Reviewer says everyone is on tonight, unlike many off nights in 1984; considers Kingswood possibly the year's best [23]
- Reviewer counts this night and the following one among the better sets of 1984 [26]
- Previous Casey Jones was August 3, 1982, 125 shows earlier [4]
- Previous Casey Jones was August 3, 1982, 125 shows earlier [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-06-26.127526.schoeps.oade.BCE.flac16**: taped by Doug Oade; transferred by Dave Usborne; source: Source from Doug Oade: Schoeps cmc441 > Sony TC-D5M > Sony PCM-601ESD > Wav; Mastering by Dave Usborne: Izotpoe RX Advanced Declick and Spectral Repair used… [1]
- **gd1984-06-26.beyerm88.holbrook.burke.81975.flac24**: taped by Kyle Holbrook; transferred by Tim Burke; source: Beyer M88 > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX90 (No Dolby) [4]. Also: Beyer M88 recording by Holbrook and Burke, 24-bit FLAC; tape flips after Tennessee Jed, Man Smart, Woman Smarter, Don't Need Love [4]
- **gd1984-06-26.beyerm88.holbrook.burke.81741.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Kyle Holbrook; transferred by Tim Burke; source: Beyer M88 > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX90 (No Dolby) [5]. Also: Beyer M88 recording by Holbrook and Burke; tape flips after Tennessee Jed, Man Smart, Woman Smarter, Don't Need Love [5]
- **gd1984-06-26.179126.senn.441.strizak.flac2448**: taped by Tom Strizak; transferred by Tom Strizak; source: Tom Strizak’s Master Analog Cassettes: (2) Senn. 441’s @ approx. 7’ high standard stereo configuration > 2nd in line Sony TC-D5M (2 Maxell XLII 90 /Dolby-B 2nd… [6]. Also: Sennheiser 441 recording by Strizak; tape flips healed in Looks Like Rain and Drums [6]
- **gd84-06-26.sbd.braverman.20324.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>PCM>DAT>CD>SHN. Tennessee Jed and Day Job are patched from an audience recording via Ray Hansen, encoded by Peter Braverman [16]

Rarity of Casey Jones as show opener makes the show special as a collection item

Weir makes a cryptic comment before Women Are Smarter
He's Gone runs over seventeen minutes
Reviewer says everyone is on tonight, unlike many off nights in 1984; considers Kingswood possibly the year's best
Security was lax during the first night's first set; fans repeatedly hopped the fence and returned from their car
Casey Jones was a rare treat for this attendee
Reviewer counts this night and the following one among the better sets of 1984
Early 6pm showtime; attendee recalls sound and lighting problems at the start, slow getting going, then lots of energy
